thread:
sasha: Quick heads-up — after merging PR #4826 (fp8 kernels) I’m seeing a clear int4 throughput regression on 13B when batch sizes >8. Can someone run a targeted sweep and sanity-check quality? :eyes:

kenji: Which benchmark exactly? perf (tokens/s / p50 latency) or quality (ppl/ROUGE)? Need exact config to reproduce.

sasha: Perf + quality. Repro command below (what I used). I grabbed traces with tracing=basic.

marta: Paste the command and a short log snippet and I can kick off perf-runs on the dedicated pool.

sasha: Command I ran locally:

```bash
./tools/quant-bench \
  --model redwood-13b \
  --quant int4,fp8 \
  --batch-sizes 1,4,8,16 \
  --seq-len 1024 \
  --iters 200 \
  --workset eval_prompts_small.jsonl \
  --export traces_fp8_int4.tar
```

And a distilled log: 
```
[13B][int4][b=8]  avg p50=158ms tokens/s=920
[13B][int4][b=16] avg p50=210ms tokens/s=620  <-- regression vs pre-PR: ~-24%
[13B][fp8][b=16] avg p50=165ms tokens/s=880
```

kenji: Interesting that fp8 at b=16 is fine but int4 suffers. Could be batching scheduling or a fallback path. Any kernel-selection debug output?

aleks: Might be continuous-batching threshold or kernel tiling switch at >8. Try setting env REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX=8 to force old path and see if perf matches. Also enable verbose kernel logging: `export REDWOOD_KERN_DEBUG=1`.

devon: I can profile KV-cache and inter-shard comms. Will run perf job on dedicated-1 and attach perf flamegraphs. ETA ~45m.

perf-ci-bot: Queued perf run 1763360001 for redwood-13b int4/fp8 sweep, pool=dedi-prod-1.

marta: Running the same command on dedi now. I'll pin quant config to int4-only first then fp8-only, then mixed. Will upload traces to /runs/1763360001.

sasha: Also want a quick quality check — run eval harness against our prompt set (30 prompts) and compare ppl and approx ROUGE. Example diffs I saw: int4 @ b=16 -> ppl +1.8 vs baseline (float16), fp8 @ b=16 -> ppl +0.4. Not huge but worth checking edgecases.

kenji: If ppl change correlates with throughput drop, maybe extra corrective decoding steps (fallbacks) are being triggered under certain memory pressure patterns. Can you paste decoder logs with "token_fallback" occurrences?

sasha: Found some lines: `decoder: kv_cache_miss -> fallback_to_host_copy` about 12 times during b=16 int4 run.

aleks: That sounds like quantized KV cache path hitting a corner-case. Two guesses: (1) quantized KV page alignment changed with fp8 patch, (2) a new sync barrier got introduced for certain kernel combos.

devon: My profile shows a 45ms stall at the shard-merge step for int4 b=16 that does not appear for fp8 b=16. Attaching snippet: `stall: gpu_wait_for_peer memcpy 45ms`.

marta: Dedi runs finished: traces uploaded -> /runs/1763360001/traces_fp8_int4.tar. Summary: int4 b=16 tokens/s=610, fp8 b=16 tokens/s=875, int4 b<=8 matches baseline.

kenji: Good repro. Next steps: (a) dump kernel selection flags from run, (b) reproduce with REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX=8 toggle, (c) run microkernel stress test (single step with varying tiles). I'll open a tracking issue.

sasha: Filing issue now with links to traces and logs. Please add PR numbers if you test fixes.

aleks: Quick mitigation: set default batch cap for int4 model profiles to 8 until we fix kernel selection. That buys time for customers.

marta: Done — added model-profile override for redwood-13b:int4 to cap to 8 in staging. Will promote to prod after QA.

devon: I'll follow up with flamegraphs and the exact memcpy callstack in the issue.

perf-ci-bot: Perf run 1763360001 completed. Artifacts: /ci/artifacts/1763360001/{traces,flamegraphs,logs}.

kenji: Thanks all. Who wants to own the postmortem? I can draft a short triage doc if nobody else takes it.

sasha: Kenji please — short doc with reproduction steps, root-cause hypotheses, mitigation (batch cap), and next PR. Add check to the regression-suite to run int4 b=16 for redwood-13b so this doesn't slip again. :thumbsup:

kenji: Will do. I’ll create the doc and link CI artifacts. Expect a draft in ~2h.

aleks: Also add a quick unit test that asserts no host-fallbacks for the quantized KV cache on the micro-kernel runner.

sasha: Great. Thanks everyone. Reopen if you find contradictory data. :rocket:
